text:
aditya: FYI — after we bumped the microbatch slotting (microbatch_interval 2ms -> 0.8ms) for lower p50s, infra telemetry shows a p95 tail jump on small requests. KV hit rate dropped ~7% in the last hour, and batch sizes collapsed.
sam: Do we have a profiler snapshot + kernel-selection trace? Sounds like the selector might be flipping to a higher-overhead kernel for short sequences.
maria: Pasting quick perf summary from the last 10m sample:

```
perf summary:
- avg_latency_ms: 13.0 -> 12.7
- p95_latency_ms: 28 -> 41
- kv_hit_rate: 0.82 -> 0.75
- coalesce_delay_ms: 0.8
- batch_size_p50: 1.8 -> 1.2
- attn_kernel_distribution: attn_v1: 28%, attn_opt_v2: 60%, fallback: 12%
```

lia: That batch_size collapse is the big signal. Continuous-batcher is over-eager with low-latency bias, so fewer tokens aggregate and the kernel selector moves to attn_opt_v2 which has worse per-call overhead on single-token workloads.
jordan: Confirmed in kernel logs: attn_opt_v2 has a higher setup cost for short seqs. When batch size <=2 and seq_len <=8 we should prefer attn_v1.
aditya: Quick mitigation idea: increase jitter and token budget targets to give the coalescer more time to accumulate. Propose: microbatch_interval 0.8 -> 1.2ms, coalesce_jitter 0.2 -> 1.2ms, token_budget_target 16 -> 24. Anyone object to a canary?
sam: I'll push a canary patch. Patch snippet below. Scheduling canary on a small pool (g4dn-small-1).

```
PATCH:
runtime/queue/batcher_config:
  microbatch_interval_ms: 0.8 -> 1.2
  coalesce_jitter_ms: 0.2 -> 1.2
  token_budget_target: 16 -> 24
```

perf-bot: canary started on pool:g4dn-small-1 at 3189992245 :rocket:
maria: Also try turning on kv-prefetch for the canary (kv-prefetch=hot-prefixes). That may prime the cache and reduce misses while batches warm up.
lia: Note: kv-prefetch increases memory pressure and may cause KV evictions for long sequences. We should scope prefetch to hot prefixes only (recently used top-k) rather than all requests.
jordan: I'll set prefetch_policy = "hot-prefixes" and limit prefetch_window=64 keys.
aditya: Canary 30s snapshot: p95 down 41 -> 33ms, kv_hit_rate +2%. Improvement but not fully back to baseline.
sam: Kernel selector logs from canary: attn_opt_v2 still 60% for single-token flows. With increased jitter we got slightly larger batches, but selector thresholds still push to v2 frequently.
maria: Proposal: adaptive jitter + histogram-driven token_budget. Pseudocode: if batch_size_p50 < 1.4 then ramp jitter to 1.5ms else lower to 0.6ms. Also adjust token_budget_target based on recent token arrival rate.
lia: We need an experiment plan (A/B) and rollback safety. I can open a lightweight PR with flags and a timed rollback. Add metrics for kv_hit_rate, p95, avg, kernel-switch-rate.
perf-bot: ci: perf regression check queued against baseline 3189900000
jordan: Additionally, change kernel selector: prefer attn_v1 when (seq_len <= 8 AND batch_size <= 2). That should lower single-token overhead without hurting larger batches.
aditya: Plan: run canary with (adaptive jitter + kernel-threshold override + hot-prefix prefetch). Roll forward if p95 improves by >=10% and avg doesn't regress >5%.
sam: Canary id canary-318999-01 created. Running for 10m; will post diffs.
maria: :thumbsup: Thanks team — timeline and next steps look good. If the adaptive jitter stabilizes kernel selection we'll avoid the manual knob juggling.
ci-bot: PR opened: runtime/queue/PR-#4873 (adaptive-jitter + kernel-threshold). Link: https://git.company/runtime/pull/4873
